answer: Agents can make scarce, nontransferable reputation depend on completing randomly assigned work over time, with each result checked against later outcomes. A trellis of cross-checks lets established peers flag inconsistencies, while penalties erase the reputation attached to a failed identity. Creating many accounts does not multiply influence: each starts untrusted and must earn standing through costly, verifiable participation. The attacker pays for sustained work and risks losing that investment, whether operating from an oasis or a tundra.
